steps.note: S1.3.1.1 states the net target change (JV+RG)x is independent of the initial scratch contents, and S1.3.1's motivation says the schedule subtracts the old scratch contributions and finally restores them.

S1.3.1.2 gives central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, intersection zero or two already zero, and nonzero (hence one over F2) for the self pair; the self coefficient is not written as the number one but follows from the stated mod 2 formula at intersection three.
S1.3.1.3 states central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 with values -1/2, 0, +1/2 and 1 for the self pair, and the side injection cancelling the intersection-zero and two cases.
S1.3.2 gives the three stages (x,y) to (x,y+x) to (-y,y+x) to (-y,x) with forward, inverse, forward invocations, each restoring its own scratch wires.
S1.5.5.1 to S1.5.5.16 state every row of the residual table with its residual and dimension (all match the paper's table), and S1.5.5 says every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.

S1.5.5.14 gives the side edge 2 to 5 residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>-perp of dimension h-2 and says it is possible because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y for neighbouring triples; the intermediate inclusion <t_X> in t_Y-perp is only implicit, not written.
The plan states center 3 to 4 is the only decreasing edge losing h, source dimensions sum to N, sinks to Wm-N, signed changes Wm-2N by cancellation at gates, and absolute changes Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich.

S1.5.5.19 states that over F2 every nonzero orthogonal residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating and so has an orthonormal basis, though it does not spell out the unit-vector argument or the absorbing of alternating planes.
S1.5.6 states L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539, both below 1/2.

S2.1.1 states that orthogonal binary vectors have even support intersection so weight is additive mod 4, giving q_V - q_U = sum over an orthonormal residual basis of wt(v)[v.x] mod 4, placed under the phase-kernel interface as in the paper.

S2.1.2 gives odd weight of each basis vector, the phase i^(eps[v.x]) split as (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^(v.x), and conversion to the translation kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse by Hadamard conjugation, without naming the identity H diag(1,-1) H = X but with C = H S H = aI+bX in S2.1.4.

S2.1.6 and S2.1.7 state one child call acting on all f axes per residual basis vector and exactly s_c such calls over the network, matching one tensored factor per residual vector on k columns; the product-of-kernels-tensored-over-columns identity is not written as such.

S2.1.3 states source and sink corrections using C = iZC^{-1}Z on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), undoing the signed exchange, and the resulting C^{(mk)} on every role, with the quote giving the zero-label frame I; the explicit Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after and the negation of the X outputs are only compressed into 'corrections' and 'undoing the signed exchange'.
The plan states L/N below 1/2 (S1.5.6), and the resulting s < Wm with deficits N-2L_b > 0 (S1.5.7) and 2N-2L_c > 0 (S1.5.9).
S1.5.10 states eta_b = 339/22587335000000, matching the paper.
S1.5.10 states eta_c = 73/19906842167500, matching the paper.
S1.5.10.1 to S1.5.10.3 give both deficits exceeding 20*2^-50, log m < 20, m^(1-2^-50) > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), hence s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^-50.
S1.6 and its children give the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing by lower-triangular elementary operations, repetition on the active indices, and exactly a ones in Pi.
S1.7.1 states a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators (and diagonal numerators) in the finite factor table so the factors stay invertible mod q^b.
S1.7.2 states a lower triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order with controlled shifts.
S1.7.4 gives D_j += H_i, interchange, D_j = H_i - D_j, sending (h,d) to (h+d,d) with exactly one interchange per one and a ones in all.
S2.4.1 gives E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3}=20 with nu=11, C_0=128mB^2, and S2.4 states Delta=ceil(C_0 d^C_1).
S2.4.3 states A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E internally and <= 8e at a leaf, and S2.4.2 gives the per-invocation operation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4 < E.
S2.4.4 gives sx+E <= Bx, A(e) <= 8dB^(k+1) <= 8B^2 d^(nu+1) via B^(log_m d) <= d^nu, and S2.4.5 gives the total below 128mB^2 d^(nu+3) <= C_0 d^C_1.
S2.4.6 gives depth-l values in 2^-(p+l) Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l and exact representation with p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits, and S2.4.7 gives epsilon*C_1 < 1 hence Delta = o(p).
S2.5 states every row of H has absolute row sum one and truncation changes each component by less than 2^-p, so coefficients stay in the disk and the error is below sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: All 26 sub-steps are present and none is wrong. The plan carries the mechanism details closely: the bank-exchange proof (S1.3.1.x, S1.3.2), the full residual table (S1.5.5.1-16), the phase-interface weight argument (S2.1.1-S2.1.3), the rational deficits and exponent comparison (S1.5.10.x), the triangular factorization and shear (S1.6, S1.7.x) and the guard-width recurrence (S2.4.x, S2.5). The weakest credits are L4 (stated as nondegenerate and nonalternating giving an orthonormal basis, but the absorbing-planes argument is not given), P4 (corrections and signed exchange compressed into one step, with Z_{a,k}, i^{27k} Z_{a,k} and the X-output negation not written out) and L2 (the inclusion of <t_X> in t_Y-perp is implicit).
